newsitem.title: GERMANY: Serb accused of genocide on trial in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Serb accused of genocide on trial in Germany.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb went on trial in Germany on Friday on war crimes charges including genocide, accused of leading a death squad which massacred Moslems in 1992.
Nikola Jorgic, 50, is also charged with causing bodily harm and deprivation of liberty.
Another Serb went on trial on Tuesday in Munich for aiding murder and genocide, the first such trial in Germany since the Nuremberg Tribunal in 1945 where Nazi leaders were convicted of war crimes.
Jorgic, who had been living in the German city of Bochum, denies the charges. His lawyers say the case is one of mistaken identity because they say Jorgic was in prison at the time.
Jorgic looked pale as he was led into the court in handcuffs and refused to testify, saying the case was not the responsibility of the German legal system.
"I have lived in Germany since 1969, got married, had a child and worked hard here. But all these reasons do not justify my sitting in this court," Jordic told the court.
"Only the Hague tribunal or a court in Serbia are relevant (to try) these crimes..A person can defend himself against everything except for the policies of world powers," he said.
But Judge Guenter Kranz said German courts could hear genocide cases regardless of where the crime took place.
Prosecutors allege Jorgic led a group of Serb nationalists from May to September 1992 and took part in at least 14 instances of "ethnic cleansing".
In one incident, Jorgic and an accomplice fired machine guns at a group of Moslems in the town of Grapska in June 1992, killing 22 people, prosecutors say.
German officials say they offered the case to the United Nations war crimes tribunal in the Hague but agreed to take it on themselves because the tribunal was overloaded with work.
In Munich Novislav Djajic was accused of taking part in a June 1992 raid in which 14 Moslem men were killed and 15 others taken prisoner, and never seen again.
